401911642.summary: Nakamura is the clear pick with superior record and recent form, but Schmid's size advantage and KO power create enough finish risk to make the heavy favorite unsuitable for parlays.
reasons: Nakamura's 8-1 record with five straight wins vastly outclasses Schmid's 4-3 with inconsistent results
Nakamura finishes via KO/TKO in 7 of 8 wins; Schmid has been stopped twice by KO in losses, matching Nakamura's primary method
Schmid owns a 3-inch height and 1-inch reach advantage at featherweight, giving him a puncher's chance despite inferior record
Capper consensus at 87.3% and -325 pricing align with Nakamura's dominance, but the 79.2% KO call suggests volatility unsuitable for parlays

401928113.summary: Lucas Fernando's recent finishing streak and significant reach advantage support the consensus, but the -325 price is steep for a three-round light heavyweight fight where variance remains high.
reasons: Fernando is 5-0 in last five with 3 TKOs in last three fights; Elekana's last five shows more mixed results with decision wins
Fernando's 80.5 reach versus Elekana's 77.5 gives meaningful advantage in striking range at LHW
Fernando's 8 KO wins and recent finishing form align with 58.7% method call for KO/TKO, but -325 moneyline limits margin of safety
Elekana's southpaw stance and submission wins provide tactical intrigue, but he has not finished an opponent in almost two years of his recent run

401928115.summary: Silva's recent decision consistency and grappling depth favor her over a striker coming off a brutal KO loss, but the -220 price is steep for a 3-round prelim with finish risk.
reasons: Silva 2-1 decisions in last three, Fernandes lost last fight by KO and showed no defensive adjustments in recent tape
Silva's BJJ and wrestling should control Fernandes's southpaw striking on the mat; decisions comprise 63% of Silva's wins vs 56% for Fernandes
Moneyline price -220 reflects consensus but overvalues in a short format where one mistake (especially by the favored grappler) changes everything; decision met

401928116.summary: Milošević is a dominant rising prospect on a five-fight win streak facing a 38-year-old veteran in sharp decline, but the -475 moneyline is overpriced for a 3-round bantamweight fight where finish risk always exists.
reasons: Milošević is 9-1 with five consecutive wins; Cachoeira is 13-9 with three straight losses including two recent finishes against her
Age and activity gap: Milošević is 30 fighting every 96 days; Cachoeira is 38 with 152 days rest and visible decline in competition level
Milošević's KO rate (4 of 9 wins) and aggressive recent finishes (KO in last two fights) align with the 54.3% consensus method call, but short odds make moneyli
The -475 reflects certainty the market should not assign to a single fight; even heavy favourites lose rounds or face judges in shortened formats

401928117.summary: Ko is the favored pick despite heavy juice, but his recent decision-heavy form and Turman's submission losses suggest this goes to the cards rather than a Ko finish as the method call suggests.
reasons: Ko is 4-1 in his last five with only one decision loss; Turman is 2-3 in his last five with three decision losses, suggesting a declining fighter
Ko's 6 KO wins versus 0 submission wins show he finishes via strikes, but his last five wins are all decisions, contradicting the 53% Ko/TKO method consensus
The -700 moneyline is steep juice for a prelim welterweight; Ko by decision offers better value than his moneyline or the speculative KO call

401928118.summary: Souza's youth, size, reach, and recent activity favor him despite Parsons' current form, but the consensus method call (Decision) combined with inconsistent finish rates on both sides and a price that doesn't compensate for the risks make this a modest lean rather than a strong conviction.
reasons: Souza has significant physical advantages: 6 inches of reach, 10 years younger, and fresh off a recent fight versus Parsons' 1200+ day layoff despite his hot st
Parsons' recent wins are impressive (3 straight KOs/decisions) but come against lower-ranked competition; Souza's record is cleaner at 9-1 with knockout power.
The capper consensus at 74.6% for Souza is reasonable but the method call (Decision at 46.9%) suggests the model has reservations about a clean finish, which re

401928119.summary: Smith is the heavy favourite with a perfect recent record, physical advantages, and a style that fits the method consensus, but -300 is too steep for a 24-year-old with only 10 pro fights against a veteran who wins by decision.
reasons: Smith's 10-1 record with five straight wins and recent finishes (KO, sub) shows current form, while Grant at 40 is slowing and has relied on decisions lately
Smith has a 2-inch reach advantage and is 16 years younger, material edges in a three-round bantamweight contest
The consensus correctly identifies a decision outcome as most likely (53.3%), fitting Smith's mixed finishing rate, but -300 moneyline underprices Grant's exper
Grant's last five include two submissions taken, but his BJJ pedigree and recent wrestling-heavy decisions suggest he can survive three rounds, making the odds

401928120.summary: Magomedov's undefeated record, recent finish power, and slight size advantage justify the consensus lean, but his limited resume and the reasonable price on Delano's experience prevent high conviction.
reasons: Magomedov is 11-0 with 11 finishes (5 KO, 6 sub) versus Delano's mixed 17-3 record with more decisions; pure finishing rate favors B
Delano's last five wins all by decision suggest he may lack finishing power at featherweight, making him vulnerable to a finisher
Magomedov is fresher (138 days vs 215) and fighting at a level where youth and undefeated record matter on prelims, but his competition quality is unproven
The moneyline odds (-110 vs +105) are too close to make Magomedov a reliable parlay piece given his inexperience

401932011.summary: Kondratavičius is the clear pick with superior record, recent form, and physical advantages, but the consensus KO method call is too narrow and the -285 price creates parlay risk.
reasons: Kondratavičius 9-1 vs Petroski 13-7 with four straight wins vs three straight losses for opponent
Size advantage (2 inches reach) and orthodox stance against switch fighter at age 27 vs 35
Kondratavičius 6 KO wins in 9 fights shows finishing power but Petroski durable enough to survive early rounds
Petroski's three recent losses all by finish (two KOs, one submission) suggests vulnerability but consensus 93.8% KO call ignores his decision losses

401932012.summary: Degli's recent form, finish rate, and reach advantage support the consensus lean, but the -230 price is steep for a flyweight matchup with finish risk.
reasons: Degli is 5-0 in last five with three finishes in last three fights; Raposo is 2-3 in last five with mixed results
Degli's 9 KO wins and 5 subs (14 of 18 wins) show consistent finishing ability; Raposo has only 4 KOs and 3 subs in 11 wins
Degli has 2.5 inch reach advantage at flyweight, a meaningful edge for distance control
Raposo is 138 days out; Degli just 44 days out, suggesting sharper recent conditioning

401932715.summary: Cortes Acosta's recent decision losses to elite competition and Walker's inconsistency at 34 support the favourite, but the consensus KO call conflicts with both fighters' recent patterns and the price is steep.
reasons: Cortes Acosta is 7-4 by decision versus 9-0 by KO; recent losses to Blaydes and Volkov went to cards, not finishes
Walker's last five is WLWLL with only one KO in last three fights; he lost to Reyes by decision after a split, showing vulnerability to better wrestling and pos
The 81.2% consensus on KO/TKO finish overstates likelihood when Cortes Acosta's true win pattern favours decisions and -225 pricing lacks value for a finish bet
At 34 with 33 days rest, Walker shows wear; Cortes Acosta at 35 with elite recent opposition (Blaydes, Volkov) is battle-tested despite losses

401932716.summary: Lorenço's perfect record, explosive finishing power, and stylistic advantages over a chinny, inconsistent opponent warrant backing him, but his limited sample size and Petersen's veteran grit prevent maximum confidence.
reasons: Lorenço is 8-1 with five straight wins and 75% finish rate (6 KO, 1 sub); Petersen is 11-5 with inconsistent results and three KO losses suggesting vulnerabilit
Lorenço freshly finished two opponents by KO in R1; Petersen just came off a R1 submission loss and showed vulnerability to pressure strikers like Petrino
Height/reach advantage (6'2" vs 6'1", 76" vs 74") and Chute Boxe striking pedigree favors Lorenço against a southpaw boxer who lacks elite wrestling or submissi
Capper consensus at 55.7% lean with KO method emphasis (52.3%) aligns with record analysis, but 8-1 record is still small sample for 5-confidence pricing

401933235.summary: Bashi's submission prowess and grappling credentials align with capper consensus, but the -500 price is steep for a prelim featherweight, and Calderon's recent submission streak and size advantage create real finish risk.
reasons: Bashi 6 submission wins vs Calderon 6, but Bashi's last two losses were decisions suggesting Calderon's wrestling/control could neutralize the submission game
Calderon fighting on short rest (34 days) but on a three-fight win streak with two first-round finishes, showing sharpness
The -500 moneyline prices in nearly zero upset equity despite featherweight volatility; Calderon's 5-inch height and reach advantage at 145 lbs is non-trivial
Capper consensus submission call (78.9%) is strong and matches Bashi's record, making it the highest-conviction angle

401911642.summary: Nakamura is the clear pick with superior record and recent form, but Schmid's size advantage and KO power create enough finish risk to make the heavy favorite unsuitable for parlays.
reasons: Nakamura's 8-1 record with five straight wins vastly outclasses Schmid's 4-3 with inconsistent results
Nakamura finishes via KO/TKO in 7 of 8 wins; Schmid has been stopped twice by KO in losses, matching Nakamura's primary method
Schmid owns a 3-inch height and 1-inch reach advantage at featherweight, giving him a puncher's chance despite inferior record
Capper consensus at 87.3% and -325 pricing align with Nakamura's dominance, but the 79.2% KO call suggests volatility unsuitable for parlays

401928111.summary: Suarez's superior wrestling and recent form justify the favourite, but Jandiroba's submission prowess and price warrant caution in parlays.

401928113.summary: Lucas Fernando's recent finishing streak and significant reach advantage support the consensus, but the -325 price is steep for a three-round light heavyweight fight where variance remains high.
reasons: Fernando is 5-0 in last five with 3 TKOs in last three fights; Elekana's last five shows more mixed results with decision wins
Fernando's 80.5 reach versus Elekana's 77.5 gives meaningful advantage in striking range at LHW
Fernando's 8 KO wins and recent finishing form align with 58.7% method call for KO/TKO, but -325 moneyline limits margin of safety
Elekana's southpaw stance and submission wins provide tactical intrigue, but he has not finished an opponent in almost two years of his recent run

401928115.summary: Silva's recent decision consistency and grappling depth favor her over a striker coming off a brutal KO loss, but the -220 price is steep for a 3-round prelim with finish risk.
reasons: Silva 2-1 decisions in last three, Fernandes lost last fight by KO and showed no defensive adjustments in recent tape
Silva's BJJ and wrestling should control Fernandes's southpaw striking on the mat; decisions comprise 63% of Silva's wins vs 56% for Fernandes
Moneyline price -220 reflects consensus but overvalues in a short format where one mistake (especially by the favored grappler) changes everything; decision met

401928116.summary: Milošević is a dominant rising prospect on a five-fight win streak facing a 38-year-old veteran in sharp decline, but the -475 moneyline is overpriced for a 3-round bantamweight fight where finish risk always exists.
reasons: Milošević is 9-1 with five consecutive wins; Cachoeira is 13-9 with three straight losses including two recent finishes against her
Age and activity gap: Milošević is 30 fighting every 96 days; Cachoeira is 38 with 152 days rest and visible decline in competition level
Milošević's KO rate (4 of 9 wins) and aggressive recent finishes (KO in last two fights) align with the 54.3% consensus method call, but short odds make moneyli
The -475 reflects certainty the market should not assign to a single fight; even heavy favourites lose rounds or face judges in shortened formats

401928117.summary: Ko is the favored pick despite heavy juice, but his recent decision-heavy form and Turman's submission losses suggest this goes to the cards rather than a Ko finish as the method call suggests.
reasons: Ko is 4-1 in his last five with only one decision loss; Turman is 2-3 in his last five with three decision losses, suggesting a declining fighter
Ko's 6 KO wins versus 0 submission wins show he finishes via strikes, but his last five wins are all decisions, contradicting the 53% Ko/TKO method consensus
The -700 moneyline is steep juice for a prelim welterweight; Ko by decision offers better value than his moneyline or the speculative KO call

401928118.summary: Souza's youth, size, reach, and recent activity favor him despite Parsons' current form, but the consensus method call (Decision) combined with inconsistent finish rates on both sides and a price that doesn't compensate for the risks make this a modest lean rather than a strong conviction.
reasons: Souza has significant physical advantages: 6 inches of reach, 10 years younger, and fresh off a recent fight versus Parsons' 1200+ day layoff despite his hot st
Parsons' recent wins are impressive (3 straight KOs/decisions) but come against lower-ranked competition; Souza's record is cleaner at 9-1 with knockout power.
The capper consensus at 74.6% for Souza is reasonable but the method call (Decision at 46.9%) suggests the model has reservations about a clean finish, which re

401928119.summary: Smith is the heavy favourite with a perfect recent record, physical advantages, and a style that fits the method consensus, but -300 is too steep for a 24-year-old with only 10 pro fights against a veteran who wins by decision.
reasons: Smith's 10-1 record with five straight wins and recent finishes (KO, sub) shows current form, while Grant at 40 is slowing and has relied on decisions lately
Smith has a 2-inch reach advantage and is 16 years younger, material edges in a three-round bantamweight contest
The consensus correctly identifies a decision outcome as most likely (53.3%), fitting Smith's mixed finishing rate, but -300 moneyline underprices Grant's exper
Grant's last five include two submissions taken, but his BJJ pedigree and recent wrestling-heavy decisions suggest he can survive three rounds, making the odds

401928120.summary: Magomedov's undefeated record, recent finish power, and slight size advantage justify the consensus lean, but his limited resume and the reasonable price on Delano's experience prevent high conviction.
reasons: Magomedov is 11-0 with 11 finishes (5 KO, 6 sub) versus Delano's mixed 17-3 record with more decisions; pure finishing rate favors B
Delano's last five wins all by decision suggest he may lack finishing power at featherweight, making him vulnerable to a finisher
Magomedov is fresher (138 days vs 215) and fighting at a level where youth and undefeated record matter on prelims, but his competition quality is unproven
The moneyline odds (-110 vs +105) are too close to make Magomedov a reliable parlay piece given his inexperience

401932011.summary: Kondratavičius is the clear pick with superior record, recent form, and physical advantages, but the consensus KO method call is too narrow and the -285 price creates parlay risk.
reasons: Kondratavičius 9-1 vs Petroski 13-7 with four straight wins vs three straight losses for opponent
Size advantage (2 inches reach) and orthodox stance against switch fighter at age 27 vs 35
Kondratavičius 6 KO wins in 9 fights shows finishing power but Petroski durable enough to survive early rounds
Petroski's three recent losses all by finish (two KOs, one submission) suggests vulnerability but consensus 93.8% KO call ignores his decision losses

401932012.summary: Degli's recent form, finish rate, and reach advantage support the consensus lean, but the -230 price is steep for a flyweight matchup with finish risk.
reasons: Degli is 5-0 in last five with three finishes in last three fights; Raposo is 2-3 in last five with mixed results
Degli's 9 KO wins and 5 subs (14 of 18 wins) show consistent finishing ability; Raposo has only 4 KOs and 3 subs in 11 wins
Degli has 2.5 inch reach advantage at flyweight, a meaningful edge for distance control
Raposo is 138 days out; Degli just 44 days out, suggesting sharper recent conditioning

401932715.summary: Cortes Acosta's recent decision losses to elite competition and Walker's inconsistency at 34 support the favourite, but the consensus KO call conflicts with both fighters' recent patterns and the price is steep.
reasons: Cortes Acosta is 7-4 by decision versus 9-0 by KO; recent losses to Blaydes and Volkov went to cards, not finishes
Walker's last five is WLWLL with only one KO in last three fights; he lost to Reyes by decision after a split, showing vulnerability to better wrestling and pos
The 81.2% consensus on KO/TKO finish overstates likelihood when Cortes Acosta's true win pattern favours decisions and -225 pricing lacks value for a finish bet
At 34 with 33 days rest, Walker shows wear; Cortes Acosta at 35 with elite recent opposition (Blaydes, Volkov) is battle-tested despite losses

401932716.summary: Lorenço's perfect record, explosive finishing power, and stylistic advantages over a chinny, inconsistent opponent warrant backing him, but his limited sample size and Petersen's veteran grit prevent maximum confidence.
reasons: Lorenço is 8-1 with five straight wins and 75% finish rate (6 KO, 1 sub); Petersen is 11-5 with inconsistent results and three KO losses suggesting vulnerabilit
Lorenço freshly finished two opponents by KO in R1; Petersen just came off a R1 submission loss and showed vulnerability to pressure strikers like Petrino
Height/reach advantage (6'2" vs 6'1", 76" vs 74") and Chute Boxe striking pedigree favors Lorenço against a southpaw boxer who lacks elite wrestling or submissi
Capper consensus at 55.7% lean with KO method emphasis (52.3%) aligns with record analysis, but 8-1 record is still small sample for 5-confidence pricing

401933235.summary: Bashi's submission prowess and grappling credentials align with capper consensus, but the -500 price is steep for a prelim featherweight, and Calderon's recent submission streak and size advantage create real finish risk.
reasons: Bashi 6 submission wins vs Calderon 6, but Bashi's last two losses were decisions suggesting Calderon's wrestling/control could neutralize the submission game
Calderon fighting on short rest (34 days) but on a three-fight win streak with two first-round finishes, showing sharpness
The -500 moneyline prices in nearly zero upset equity despite featherweight volatility; Calderon's 5-inch height and reach advantage at 145 lbs is non-trivial
Capper consensus submission call (78.9%) is strong and matches Bashi's record, making it the highest-conviction angle
